1lxb184:176: The first landing point for token-level observability is slow-token localization. When a token's scheduling time is abnormally high (prefill preempting decode resources), it appears at the Span level as a spike in that token's latency. Combined with batch load metrics, you can quickly determine whether it is resource interference under a PD-separated architecture or a model badcase. This is a direct way to localize BOS-token issues like "irrelevant answers."
1pgzinm:166: The cost of adding gen_ai.skill.* attributes is extremely low—just attach four string attributes to the execute_tool Span, with no new Span type required. For systems with existing OTel instrumentation, this is a zero-breaking incremental capability. On the platform side, you can aggregate by business domain based on skill name and directly export Skill-level SLA/latency distributions, without additional business instrumentation.
1tf01xl:173: A Tool is an atomic operation (send_email, query_db), an Agent is an autonomous decision unit, and a Skill is the business-functional aggregation point in between. A Skill may call multiple Tools, but its semantics is a single business intent ("process refund", "verify qualification"). The gen_ai.skill.* attributes allow observability data to be aggregated by business domain rather than technical implementation, opening a direct path from observability to business analysis.

1v7qxeo:151: Per-token granularity produces enormous data volume—a 2048-token output generates 2048 data points. LoongSuite's solution: capture Top-K candidate distribution instead of the full distribution, combine with batch load aggregation to reduce storage overhead, while retaining scheduling time as the key metric. This "downsample without losing key signals" approach is the key to engineering feasibility.

3se9sd:213: If your framework does not yet support Entry/Step Span layering, you should consider introducing it when trace span count exceeds 100. The Entry Span records the original input/output (prompt/response), and the Step Span organizes by ReAct phases; model calls, tool calls, and state transitions in each phase are attached as child spans under the corresponding Step. This structure changes trace debugging from an O(N) linear scan to an O(log N) directory lookup.

v9r6kx:219: The traditional OTel HTTP Span model cannot map long-horizon AI Agent tasks. A single ReAct loop may span hundreds of internal calls—model inference, tool selection, memory recall—all compressed into one flat trace, making troubleshooting hopeless. LoongSuite introduces Entry/Step layering: Entry Span anchors user intent at the Agent entry, Step Span expands parent-child relationships by ReAct phase, turning the trace from "a tangled mess" into "a collapsible directory tree."
